processing: Certified organic and biodynamic black tea, withered, rolled, oxidised and fired, sold in grades such as BOP; the garden also makes green tea.
harvest_season: Picked through the year; as elsewhere in Uva, the dry-weather quality season is generally most valued.
appearance_dry: Dark brown to black broken leaf, typical of Uva grades such as BOP.
appearance_liquor: Clear, bright reddish amber, typical of high-grown Uva.
taste_profile: As with other high Uva teas, expect a brisk, bright cup with a clean finish; the organic label says nothing by itself about flavour.

brewing.notes: Western-style; a broken grade such as BOP needs a shorter steep, around three minutes.

vintage_note: Sold under the estate name by specialist retailers and by Stassen, usually as black BOP-style grades plus a green tea, with organic certification on the label. As usual for Ceylon, it is not a vintage tea: buy recent manufacture and drink within a year or two.
description:
Idulgashinna, also spelled Idalgashinna, is an organic tea garden in the high Uva country near Haputale. It belongs to Stassen, and what sets it apart is less a particular taste than its place in the story of organic tea.

The garden sits high: sources give about 1,800 metres, or a range of roughly 5,000 to 6,000 feet, classed as Uva High. The leaf goes through standard black tea making, with organic and biodynamic farming being the difference.

Expect the character typical of high Uva, brisk and bright. Brew it Western-style with water just off the boil, and take a little off the time for broken grades, which turn sharp quickly.

You will see several spellings when shopping, so search for all of them. It is sold as black tea and as green; check which one you are buying, and the certification on the pack.
history:
Accounts of its beginnings differ. Retail sources say the estate began in 1984, while another ties its heritage to the late 19th century.

Stassen, its owner, presents itself as a pioneer of certified organic tea. Its first international certification is variously dated 1987 and 1989, and the garden is described as biodynamic since 1999, with Demeter certification a first for a Sri Lankan producer. These claims come largely from the company and its retailers.
